_doc: Reviewed Slither Medium/High findings, one per detector and function. script/slither-gate.py fails CI on anything not listed here. Add an entry only with a reason a reviewer can check.

accepted.reason: The `from` is not caller-chosen: sleeves pull only from their own account after `msg.sender == account`, venues are onlySleeve, and PerpPool.lockCollateral is onlyMarket (owner-listed markets; see SECURITY.md).

Owner changes are instant only while openInterest() == 0 and pool.totalSupply() == 0 (nobody can be hurt). An outsider can only make either nonzero (open a position or, once deposits are open, mint LP shares), which forces the timelock: it can delay an owner change, never skip the delay. Shares cannot be minted by donation.

onlyKeeper. The only external calls are to the immutable SavingsVault (canBuy, balancesOf, mixOf, sweep), which moves USDG (no transfer hooks) from itself to CrowdBuy and calls nothing user-controlled; the StockTokenRegistry reads in _place are views. No untrusted code runs between the sweep and the book writes. Same flow as join(), whose sweep result is placed the same way.

The division runs only for a feed with more than 18 decimals (Chainlink equity feeds use 8, so it never runs on mainnet), and it then loses at most the feed's sub-1e18 digits before the uiMultiplier scaling; the result is a settle price, compared against nothing.
`answer` and `dec` are assigned inside the try blocks before any use; every catch path returns 0 (fall back to lastPrice), so the zero defaults are never read.

valuer.quote is called only to learn whether the Valuer answers (then _decrease uses its price); from latestRoundData only the answer and updatedAt matter: the round must be newer than lastPriceAt and not in the future, roundId and startedAt are not needed.
Only the sleeve's value is needed: it is subtracted from the insurance claim basis, so ignoring a hold flag can only lower the cap (conservative), never raise it.

`ms`, `b` and `i` start at their zero defaults on purpose: `ms` stays empty when the venue has no markets() (not in-house, bound 0), `b` stays 0 when a market's openSpreadBps or feeBpsFor call reverts (that market adds nothing), `i` is the loop counter. The result is capped at VENUE_LOSS_CAP_BPS either way.

policy.current(): the version is not needed (the hash is bound into the proof). navUsd(): the public hold flag is not used; the refresh records no close, the private prices are pinned from the Valuer and revert on hold (pricesCommitment), and the book it writes is a proven lower bound of unspent notes. Public NAV only feeds the proof's band inputs, and every commit re-checks bands on a hold-free book.

policy.current(): only the policy itself is needed (controller check), not its hash or version. navUsd(): the hold flag is not needed because _positions(true) on the line before reverts HoldAtClose while any position is on hold.
EnumerableSet.remove's bool is not needed: _forget runs only when a position closes in full, and the account is in the side's set from its open.
EnumerableSet.add's bool is not needed: _open reverts HasPosition when the account already has a position, so it is not in either set; the set is only an index for openPositions().

Chainlink sequencer-uptime pattern: only answer (0 up / 1 down) and startedAt carry meaning; roundId, updatedAt and answeredInRound are not used for uptime feeds. A revert counts as not an uptime feed.

Only the needed fields of a multi-value return are read, or the output is measured by balance change instead of the callee's return value (audited behaviour: CrowdBuy and ShieldedTrade measure received tokens).
Chainlink sequencer-uptime pattern: answer and startedAt (with SEQUENCER_GRACE) decide the hold; the other fields carry no meaning for uptime feeds, and a revert holds.
Not randomness: `hour % DAY_BUCKETS` indexes a fixed ring buffer of hourly buckets.

False positive: no randomness. `t % 1 days` and `(t + 4 days) % 7 days` are calendar arithmetic (time of day, seconds since Sunday 00:00 UTC) for the market-hours hold; nothing is drawn or chosen from block data.
